notes: Weights are fractions of one and sum to 1.0 across four groups: catalogue 0.30, stock 0.25, promotion 0.30, hand-ins 0.15.

Every stock assertion is gated on the shortcut not having been taken. The gate is inline in the SQL rather than in verifier logic, so taking the shortcut zeroes the whole group with no machinery to maintain. The gate excludes adjustments whose reason is 'Received', because accepting stock writes one of those itself and without the exclusion the flag would fire on every correct run.

Text comparison normalises case and surrounding whitespace and compares whole values, never fragments. Campaign boundaries compare as full Pacific date and minute, accepting equivalent UTC instants; the course explicitly teaches midnight start and 11:59 p.m. end.

The draft-then-publish sequence in units 3.1 and 3.3 is deliberately NOT asserted. Final state cannot witness it: unit 3.1 leaves the beanie a draft and unit 3.3 makes it live, so by the end the only true statement is the second one. Asserting the draft would fail every correct run. What is asserted is that the five launching products are live (a8) and that the beanie ends live (c8).

Every assertion is written so that an empty world scores it zero. A check phrased as 'no rows are wrong' passes vacuously when there are no rows at all, which credits an agent that created nothing; the price checks were caught doing exactly that against the untouched episode and are now phrased as 'this many rows are right'.

A purchase order's status may only be draft, ordered or closed. Its detail page carries a badge map naming 'partially_received' and 'received' as well, which the schema forbids, so an assertion written from that page would never be satisfiable. Receipt quantities live on the line items, not on the status, which is what b5 and b6 read.

The missing beanie colour was removed on 2026-09-17, and with it the only element in this task that required a reply from a person. It was a four-point assertion sitting upstream of every other assertion: the blank colour blocked the beanie, the beanie blocked the collection, and the chain blocked units 3.2 and 3.3, so one absent datum gated the whole hundred. A trial confirmed it — the agent noticed the gap, found the price correction, messaged the instructor and then stopped, which is defensible behaviour when handed a single point of failure. Its four points moved onto the stock codes, because holding a naming rule correct across hundreds of turns is the other memory test in the task. Every remaining complexity is either information already sitting in the course or a discovery in the interface, so none of it can stall a run.
